authored.note: Written for learners from the sources named in each block. It is an explanation, not a recording. Facts listed under each block are checked word for word against those sources.

summary.text: One agent (the caller) tells another (the callee) that authority has been delegated for a privileged action. The lab asks whether such a claim can create authority that neither agent was actually given. Its one idea: a caller or delegation claim is data, and it does not mint authority. The agent names here are labels for attribution, not authenticated identities.
facts: This lab teaches one idea: a caller/delegation claim is data. It does not mint authority.
Agent id strings are attribution, not cryptographic identity.

glance.label: What the attacker wants
glance.text: The attacker wants the delegation claim treated as a grant, so that neither agent needs the customer:read permission.
facts: The attacker wants the claim treated as a grant so neither agent needs customer:read.

glance.label: What the attacker controls
glance.text: Only the claim in the lab's closed fixture. The browser cannot choose the setting, the grants, whether anyone is verified or authenticated, or the request body.
facts: The browser does not choose profile, grants, identity_verified, authenticated, or the A2A body.

glance.label: Who is involved
glance.text: A principal (applicant-web), a caller agent (acme-agent-advisor-005) and a callee agent (acme-agent-fulfillment-006). These are names in the records, not proven identities.
facts: Identify principal applicant-web, caller acme-agent-advisor-005, callee acme-agent-fulfillment-006.

glance.label: Where the delegation boundary is
glance.text: Between the claim and the tool. Both agents are coded with the same narrow grant (lookup_policy only), and combining two agents does not add authority.
facts: Coded grants for both agents: lookup_policy / policy:read / lending-basics only.

glance.label: How the controls handle it
glance.text: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 only observes the claim and never grants anything. CTRL-MCP-001 is the sole tool decision point, and it is the one that denies the privileged request on the defended retest.

glance.label: A claimed identity is not an authenticated one
glance.text: Nothing in this lab authenticates anyone. The run record says so itself, and the lab models no OAuth, OIDC, JWT validation, SPIFFE or real agent-to-agent transport. Do not read an agent name as proof of who called.
facts: WHO AUTHENTICATED = NOT PROVEN / NOT MODELED.
No OAuth, OIDC, JWT validation, SPIFFE/SPIRE, or real A2A transport.

glance.label: What could go wrong
glance.text: On the deliberately vulnerable ATTACK setting the privileged tool ran through a labelled fail-open overlay. In the lab's own words that overlay is the failure; it is not a cryptographic identity bypass.
facts: On this labeled vulnerable experiment the overlay is the failure.

glance.label: What evidence exists
glance.text: Each run records the principal, caller and callee, the identity decision, the tool decision and the handler counts. ATTACK and RETEST carry the same request fingerprint, which is how you know the request itself did not change.
facts: Measure that ATTACK and RETEST share the same request fingerprint.

path.label: Delegation claim
path.detail: The caller says authority was delegated.

path.label: Principal, caller, callee
path.detail: Names carried in the request; attribution only.

path.label: Claim is not a grant
path.detail: A caller id does not mint a grant.

path.label: Identity classification
path.detail: CTRL-IDENTITY-001 observes the claim as untrusted. It never grants.

path.label: Tool authorization
path.detail: CTRL-MCP-001 is the sole tool decision point.

outcomes.label: DENY (defended retest)
outcomes.detail: tool_not_granted; the privileged handler does not start.
outcomes.fact: Prove RETEST CTRL-MCP-001 DENY tool_not_granted with handler 0.

outcomes.label: ALLOW (vulnerable attack setting)
outcomes.detail: A labelled fail-open overlay of the lab, not a server grant.
outcomes.fact: Prove ATTACK overlay fail-open at CTRL-MCP-001 with lookup_customer_tier handler 1.

path.label: Privileged tool
path.detail: lookup_customer_tier on cust-001 with scope customer:read, only if granted.

path.label: Evidence copy
path.detail: A copy of the telemetry goes to Splunk, which only observes.

terms.text: Saying who you are is not the same as proving it. This lab only records the claim.
Being told that authority was handed over does not make it so. Authorization is a server decision.
A name such as acme-agent-advisor-005 is a label in a record. It is not a cryptographic identity.
Two agents working together do not gain authority that neither holds alone.
OBSERVE means the control recorded the claim. It is not a permission.
The identifier that ties every event of one experiment together. Every launch gets a new one.

defender.text: Grant tools on the server, from each agent's own coded permissions. A claim, an agent name or an identity string adds nothing to them.
facts: Do not trust agent names, Splunk, or an identity string.
a caller/delegation claim is data. It does not mint authority.
